data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew word 'melech' meaning 'king' and 'yah' meaning 'God'. Milenia is a biblical name that symbolizes mercy and kindness from God. The name Milenia carries the meaning “Merciful, kind” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Milenia usually hope their child will grow to embody merciful, kind and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Milenia carries a rich historical and cultural importance for believers in the Christian faith. Milenia represents the concept of a thousand-year reign or millennium, as described in the Bible's Book of Revelation. The name exudes a sense of God's sovereignty and ultimate victory over all things, reminding us of the hope and peace that comes from trusting in His plan.
data.spiritual_significance: Milenia is a powerful name that reflects the deep spiritual truths of the Christian faith. It serves as a reminder that God is our King and He reigns over all things with mercy and kindness. The name conveys a sense of trust and hope in God's perfect plan for our lives, and serves as a source of strength and encouragement in times of trials and hardships. Milenia embodies the qualities of mercy, kindness, and God's ultimate victory, inspiring those who bear the name to live lives that are rooted in faith and reflect the love and grace of God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Milenia: A beacon of hope and new beginnings, symbolizing the arrival of a new thousand-year era in Christianity, marked by peace, love, and divine guidance.

historical_references.reference: The name Milenia is derived from the Latin word 'mille' meaning 'thousand'. It was used to denote a thousand-year period in Christian eschatology, particularly in reference to the 'Thousand Year Reign' of Christ following the Second Coming.
historical_references.time_period: Late Antiquity to Middle Ages (approximately 400-1000 AD)

historical_references.reference: Another interpretation of the name Milenia comes from the Roman numeral M for thousand and the Latin suffix -enia, meaning condition or state. In this context, Milenia represents the millennial condition or state, implying a period of unparalleled peace and prosperity under the rule of Christ.
historical_references.time_period: Various, depending on specific interpretations of millenarianism in Christian history
